description.narrative:
Transparency International Anti-Corruption Center - Armenia (TIAC) har ansökt till Sida om finansiering på totalt 7 100 000 SEK för att genomföra projektet "Institutional Support Grant" under perioden 2021-2023.
Insatsen syftar till att genom kärnstöd till TIAC stödja pågående ansträngningar för att främja god samhällsstyrning och antikorruptionspolicy genom följande mål; 1) policy och lagändring för att säkerställa transparent och ansvarsfull styrning, 2) beteendeförändring för att öka medborgarnas intolerans mot korruption; 3) uppsökande och medvetandehöjande för att påverka policyn och beteendeförändringar; 4) organisationsutveckling.
Stödet, som planeras att tillhandahållas i form av kärnstöd kommer att syfta till att möjliggöra för TIAC att bidra till Armeniens demokratiska utveckling. Insatsen kommer enbart att genomföras av TIAC, utan vidareförmedling av medel till tredje part.

Transparency International Anti-corruption Center - Armenia (TIAC) has applied to Sida for funding of 7 100 000 SEK, to carry out "Institutional Support Grant" project during the period of 2021-2023.
The intervention aims to provide core support to TIAC’s ongoing efforts in promoting good governance and anti-corruption policies through the following objectives; 1) policy and legislative change to ensure transparent and accountable governance; 2) behavioral change to enhance intolerance of citizens toward corruption; 3) outreach and awareness raising to influence the policy and behavior changes; 4) organizational development.
The support, which is planned to be provided in the form of core support, will enable TIAC to contribute to Armenia´s democratic development. The intervention will be solely implemented by TIAC, with no forwarding of funds to third parties.

TIAC Policy changes have been mostly driven by TIACs research and monitoring efforts accompanied with assistance and advocacy targeting relevant decision-making institutions and officials. In particular TIAC provided significant expert support to the Ministry of Justice in the development of the Armenian Governments Anticorruption Strategy and Its Implementation Plan for 2023-2026, which is the main document that shapes the countrys current anticorruption policy. Monitoring of international anticorruption commitments and engagement with relevant international actors was critical for the development of reports and recommendations by OECD and GRECO. TIAC developed an alternative report for assessing the progress of implementation of SDG16 and contributed to CEPA Progress Monitoring by CSOs. We also contributed to the development and monitoring of OGP 5th Action Plan. Through its expert input and advocacy, TIAC brought the need for legislative reforms to the attention of the National Assemblys Standing Committee on State and Legal Affairs, leading to critical discussions about establishing an Ethics Committee for MPs and developing a Code of Conduct. We also revived the public dialogue on constitutional amendments, addressing urgent challenges such as the stable majority principle, which distorts the system of checks and balances and threatens democratic institutions. TIACs assessment of parliamentary oversight had a significant impact as it highlighted gaps in MPs ability to hold the government accountable. Another study on the Audit Chamber prompted the need for the revision of the oversight methodology of this institution. TIACs comparative analysis of local whistleblowing legislation against the EU Whistleblower Protection Directive brought critical inefficiencies in the whistleblower protection system to the attention of the Ministry of Justice and key donor organizations. The analysis will contribute to the implementation of the Anticorruption Strategy by strengthening whistleblower protection mechanisms and enhancing overall system accountability. The assessment of the performance of Corruption Prevention Commission (CPC) led to an increased understanding of the CPCs strengths and weaknesses and paved the way for enhancing institutional improvements aimed at its increased effectiveness. A comprehensive assessment of the public procurement systems had a notable impact by providing the government with a detailed evaluation of the system's quality and effectiveness, which will assist in the current reform of public procurement. Studies of public councils, participation processes in the ministries and participation in legal drafting as well as the periodic monitoring of the civic space through CSO Meter methodology deepened the general understanding of the gaps in democratic decision-making in the country, which motivated to include a corrective measure within the Public Administration Reform. TIACs study of transparency and accountability of Yerevan municipality shed light on the state of implementation of relevant legal requirements and pointed to the gaps and needs for improvement. TIACs successful strategic litigations in cooperation with its partners - the Law Development and Protection Foundation and Civilnet Foundation, contributed to the development of the case law on access to information (such as the results of environmental inspection of the mining projects) and public participation (such as the civic oversight over the competition for running to become a member of CPC).
Behavioural changes are largely achieved through civic education and stakeholder engagement, the development of auxiliary materials and the facilitation of understanding, motivation and networking. In particular TIACs anticorruption school has raised the knowledge of 121 students, 13% (16 participants) of which were working in Armenia's anticorruption institutions, implemented their own anticorruption projects, and engaged 214 new audiences. TIACs training of 40 media professionals, support to investigative journalists and constantly provided consultations have increased the number and improved the quality of media coverage of corruption matters. The Guidebook on Political Party Finance Oversight along with training of 63 civic activists, researchers, journalists and members of political parties facilitated the understanding of the money flows in politics and boosted conversation on political corruption and the need for more integrity in politics. The Guidebook for Civics' teachers developed by TIAC, endorsed by the Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sports, expects to significantly promote the effective and comprehensive education of schoolchildren on corruption-related matters. The relevant training of 41 civic teachers had a multiplying effect, allowing anti-corruption knowledge to spread more widely among their students.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
